title: OOP Exercises
description: Practise the ideas from this Object-Oriented Programming course. Each answer has an explanation to help you learn.

exercises.question: Which property stores 24?
exercises.explanation: An object keeps related values together. A property is one named value inside the object. The result is Moon. The title property belongs to book.

exercises.question: What do parentheses after describe do?
exercises.explanation: A method is a function stored on an object. It can use this to read the object that called it. The result is Moon book. The parentheses call the method.

exercises.question: What does new Book make?
exercises.explanation: A class is a plan for making similar objects. Each object made from it is called an instance. The result is Ocean. new makes an instance and runs the constructor.

exercises.question: Does changing a.title change b.title here?
exercises.explanation: Each instance has its own properties. Changing one book does not change a different book. The result is Ocean. The two objects hold separate title values.

exercises.question: Which starting value is used when none is supplied?
exercises.explanation: A constructor sets up a new object. A default value is used when the caller leaves out an argument. The result is 0 because no starting value was supplied.

exercises.question: Which method reads the private count?
exercises.explanation: A private field starts with #. Code outside the class cannot directly read or change it. The result is 1. Callers use add and read to work with the hidden value.

exercises.question: How is the getter read?
exercises.explanation: A getter calculates a value when you read a property. You do not call it with parentheses. The result is 9. area multiplies the side by itself.

exercises.question: Which keyword creates a child class?
exercises.explanation: Inheritance lets one class extend another. The child class receives methods from its parent. The result is sound. Dog uses the inherited speak method.

exercises.question: Which speak method runs for new Dog()?
exercises.explanation: A child can replace an inherited method with its own version. This is called overriding. The result is woof. Dog supplies its own speak method.

exercises.question: What action do both objects support?
exercises.explanation: Polymorphism means different objects can answer the same method call. The caller uses the action without choosing each object type. The result is woof, meow. Each object handles speak in its own way.

exercises.question: Which relationship describes this design?
exercises.explanation: Composition gives an object another object to use. A bike has a bell; a bike is not a kind of bell. The result is ding. The bike asks its bell to do one job.

exercises.question: What is Basket responsible for here?
exercises.explanation: A class is easier to understand when it has one clear job. A basket can add prices without also drawing the whole web page. The result is 7. Basket handles prices; another part of the app can show the total.
